sources.summary: CDC's 32-slide investor day deck, released by Infratil on 16 September 2026 with its 'Data centre demand drives growth and guidance increase' announcement. Slide 8 ('Operating capacity has more than doubled over the last 18 months') says CDC 'has delivered seven large-scale data centres since FY25, all of which are now contributing meaningfully to CDC's earnings generation'. It names them as Melbourne Brooklyn 2, Sydney Eastern Creek 5 & 6, Sydney Marsden Park 1, Canberra Hume 6, Canberra Beard 1 and Auckland Hobsonville 2. Slide 9 ('Construction is progressing to meet FY27-29 deliveries') says CDC 'is well underway at all sites where customer capacity has been contracted'. It reports 'Significant progress to date on delivering CDC's Laverton campus', with the first building expected to become operational in late FY27 and buildings 2 and 3 across FY28 (these are forecasts). It also reports 'Structure of CDC's inaugural Perth data centre nearing completion'. Slide 6's campus map, which uses a legend dated as at 30 June 2026, shows Canberra Beard BE1 as operational and BE2 as future development; Melbourne Laverton LA1-LA3 as under construction; and Perth Maddington MA1 as under construction and MA2 as future development.

sources.summary: Approved minutes of the Louisa County Board of Supervisors meeting of 3 August 2026, item 'Discussion - Haley Drive/Kentucky Springs Road Intersection' (PDF pages 10-11). The County Administrator reported that traffic at the Kentucky Springs Road / Haley Drive / Johnson Road intersection 'has increased significantly due to nearby construction activity'. The Cuckoo District supervisor stated that the intersection serves residents, visitors, North Anna Power Station traffic 'and construction traffic associated with the Lake Anna Technology Campus', cited 'ongoing data center construction' among the reasons immediate action was needed, and asked VDOT, Clark and Dominion for a short-term safety plan by 13 August. Board discussion recognised that VDOT, Dominion Energy, AWS, Clark and the County all have roles, and noted that traditional traffic analyses may understate 'the unusually heavy traffic generated during construction'. The Board voted to request a VDOT safety and speed study. The same minutes (PDF page 15) record DEQ's approval of a VPDES permit for AWS to discharge non-contact cooling water from the Lake Anna Technology Campus into Sedges Creek (an ancillary water permit, not development consent). Names of individual officials are not copied.
